confirmation.label_provenance: Provisional coding-agent labels assigned before inference; not independent human adjudication.

context: Actual tools/meta.rs subject identity and identity-record snapshots; metadata identifies the subject but is not article evidence.

development.prior_holdout_status: The entire previous 72-case corpus is development in this round. Its former evaluation set is no longer held out.

excluded_before_inference.reason: Incomplete main report; mostly linked headlines and a stub.
Statistics/fixture page without a reporting body.

limitations: 18 selected previously unscored article bodies; two subject judgments per source are correlated.
Coding-agent labels; boundaries such as routine motivation, substantive offseason analysis and contract guarantee decisions need human review.
Shared publisher furniture can overlap across otherwise different articles; this is not a held-out-publisher evaluation.
This round evaluates team subjects and complete retained text, not reader durability or representative production accuracy.
No model tuning after confirmation inference; a worse candidate is retained as a failed challenger, not promoted.
Balanced paired subjects and mixed real/synthetic development data do not represent production RSS prevalence.
The 18 articles were new to scoring, drawn from a retained text pool; they were not newly fetched production URLs.
Throughput, reader durability, player/person subjects and production routing remain untested. Latency includes live Kev activity and warm inputs.
Native score reliability was not calibrated; only empirical decision thresholds were selected.
metadata_exporter_change: Reject canonical name/ID mismatches instead of silently substituting another subject name.
procedure: Equal FP and FN cost. Per-topic thresholds minimize FP+FN over 10..90 by 5; ties closest to 50 then lower cutoff. Bank chosen by total four-topic errors, then Brier.
qualitative_findings: The simpler concise-v2 question bank beat reporting-v3 on development: 17 versus 24 four-topic errors.
Fresh confirmation was weaker than the first pilot: 26 of 144 four-topic labels wrong after recalibration versus 27 with the original thresholds.
Raising availability from 0.85 to 0.90 added one miss; raising subject relevance from 0.50 to 0.55 removed two false positives. Movement and emotion decisions were unchanged.
Passing opponents, old affiliations, fixture listings and related-story links still triggered relevance.
Some current injury/return reporting, emotional reactions, contract decisions and movement denials were missed.
The combined experimental gate worsened from 4 false positives and 2 misses to 4 false positives and 3 misses; neither policy is established as a reliable acquisition gate.

recommendation.model: d1 remains an offline candidate based on the earlier matched model comparison; this round did not rerun Kev or Laya.
recommendation.next_step: Independently review labels and test the shared reader with fixed questions and thresholds before production routing.
recommendation.reason: Recalibrated entity relevance had 10 false positives among 20 negatives, despite retaining all 16 positives.
recommendation.threshold_policy: Retain both frozen policies as references; the recalibrated candidate reduced topic errors by one but worsened the experimental gate.

validation: 108 new native requests: zero failures; all four probabilities and model fingerprints validated.
72 cached baseline responses verified against exact request and metadata hashes.
Frozen corpus, bank, evaluator and analyzer checks passed before confirmation reporting.
Read-only metadata integration: a deliberately mismatched subject name and ID was rejected before any case was exported.
